html:
Robert Guiscard was a Norman adventurer who conquered most of southern Italy and became Duke of Apulia and Calabria. "Guiscard" means the cunning one.

He was one of many sons of a minor knight in Normandy, and came south around 1047 to join his brothers, who were fighting as hired soldiers for the Lombard princes and the Byzantines. He began as a raider and rose to lead the Normans of the south. In 1059 the pope made him duke, turning a band of conquerors into a lawful power.

  • With his brother Roger he began the conquest of the Muslim emirate of Sicily in 1061, taking Palermo in 1072.
  • In 1071 he took Bari, ending Byzantine rule in Italy after five centuries.
  • In 1077 he took Salerno, the last Lombard state; Benevento went to the pope.

In 1081 he crossed to the Balkans to attack the Byzantine Empire and beat Alexios I Komnenos at the Battle of Dyrrhachium. To get the Venetian fleet against him, Alexios gave Venice a Golden Bull of trade privileges. In 1084 Robert went back to Italy to rescue Pope Gregory VII from the emperor Henry IV, and his troops sacked Rome. He died of fever on a new Greek campaign in 1085.

Anna Komnene's Alexiad gives a vivid, grudging portrait of him. His son Bohemond later won Antioch in the First Crusade.
sum: Robert Guiscard was a Norman adventurer who conquered most of southern Italy and became Duke of Apulia and Calabria. "Guiscard" means the cunning one.
